title: Doppler limits `AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale`
body:
### Tested versions

- Found 4.6
- Reproduced in 4.4
- Haven't tested other versions

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

When there is active doppler effect, `AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale` is limited to the approximate range of 0.125 and 8. This happens due to these two lines:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/24333c4e3d3d420298253c5fdb04176ecbac3af9/scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp#L521-L522

`AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale` is factored into the doppler scale _before_ doppler is clamped, therefore cramping it to the approximate range above. (Approximate because if pitch_scale is set to something like `8.01` while the StreamPlayer is repidly moving away from the Listener, the resulting sound would likely be correct.)

Interestingly, the above two lines of code require the emitter to have doppler enabled and for the relative velocity of the emitter and listener to be zero. If those conditions aren't met, pitch_scale works as intended, as no clamping occurs.

Video of the MRP:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d032ed4c-8a49-4ae7-aec9-1b5572439e57

### Steps to reproduce

In the MRP:

1. Hit Play
2. Adjust pitch_scale to be well above 8. Note how it sounds correct.
3. Enable spin and doppler. Note how it drops in pitch (as it is clamped)
4. Try disabling spin or disabling doppler, one at a time. Note how when one is disabled, the pitch is correct.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[doppler_pitch_clamp_mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24219873/doppler_pitch_clamp_mrp.zip)
